anti_patterns.title: Do not lift the Kanban board/dispatcher system wholesale — it is a multi-tenant, multi-worker coding-agent swarm, not a single-host steward's subagent manager
anti_patterns.evidence: hermes_cli/kanban*.py alone is 17 files plus gateway/kanban_watchers*.py (4 files, 1379 lines) plus a dashboard plugin plus a systemd dispatcher daemon service plus a GitHub PR-acceptance workflow (hermes_cli/kanban_pr_acceptance.py) plus a board export/import format for moving boards between machines (kanban_transfer.py) plus per-profile worker roster/assignee routing (kanban_decompose.py, kanban_tools.py default_assignee). This is architecturally a multi-agent, multi-machine task board for autonomous coding-agent teams working git repos and opening PRs.
anti_patterns.why_not: Conflicts with the founder constraints directly: single-user single-host (this is designed for fleets of concurrently-dispatched worker profiles across machines), one continuous conversation with no session list (this is a persistent multi-board task list UI), and one assistant identity (this presumes named specialist worker profiles a dispatcher routes between). Lifting the daemon/board/PR-acceptance apparatus would import an entire second product's architecture rather than a mechanism.

HM05-delegation-subagents-kanban.summary: This is a two-part unit. The delegation/subagent half (agent/subagent_lifecycle.py, agent/delegation_context.py, agent/kanban_stop.py, the ten tools/delegate_tool_*.py modules, async_delegation.py, delegation_live_log.py, delegation_output_schema.py, subagent_worktree.py) is rich and battle-tested, and maps cleanly onto confirmed gaps in Halbert's SubagentManager (halbert_core/halbert_core/agents/subagent.py), which is a bare FIFO/max_concurrent=2 handle-tracker with no toolset scoping, no depth limits, no output contracts, no live logs, no durability/crash-recovery, no ownership-scoped control plane, and no steer-while-running capability, and (per the task brief) no task notifications. Nineteen concrete candidates come mostly from this half, nearly all 'absent' in Halbert today. The kanban board/dispatcher half (hermes_cli/kanban*.py's 17 files, gateway/kanban_watchers*.py's 4 files, plugins/kanban/) is architecturally a multi-tenant, multi-worker, multi-machine autonomous coding-agent task-board system (git worktrees, GitHub PR acceptance, cross-machine board export, per-profile worker routing) that conflicts directly with Halbert's founder constraints (single-user single-host, one continuous conversation with no session list, one assistant identity). I extracted the specific narrow mechanisms worth taking from it (notification-delivery robustness, structured diagnostics, live comment-injection-as-steer, the 'no second scheduler, reuse existing primitives' design principle, the goal-judge fail-open lesson) and explicitly flagged the wholesale board/swarm/PR-acceptance system as three anti-patterns rather than proposing to lift it. Full JSON also written to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-4TB-BAD-Halbert/b0e3f0dd-594e-4bec-b7ce-4859472b38f8/scratchpad/wf-oss/HM05-delegation-subagents-kanban.json.

missed_by_reader.title: Liveness is proven by PROGRESS, not by a stopwatch: a shared-thread staleness monitor replaces a wall-clock child timeout
missed_by_reader.lines: 205-268 (_Heartbeat), 632-644 (await_child docstring); with tools/delegate_tool_config.py:130-138 (_get_child_timeout) and tools/delegate_tool.py:69-75 (interval + stale thresholds)
missed_by_reader.mechanism: Hermes deliberately runs delegated children with NO hard wall-clock cap by default: _get_child_timeout's docstring says 'Failures should come from what the child does (API/tool errors, iteration budget), not a stopwatch; stuck children are caught by the heartbeat staleness monitor', and await_child confirms 'Hard timeout is off by default (result(timeout=None)); stuck children are the heartbeat's job'. Instead _Heartbeat runs on the SHARED agent.periodic_scheduler thread (explicitly 'not one daemon thread per child') every _HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL=30s and reads the child's activity summary. Progress is the disjunction of three independent signals — api_call_count advanced, current_tool changed, or last_activity_ts advanced (the third exists so a slow model wait, which refreshes last_activity_ts via the direct_api_call heartbeat, never looks idle). Only while one advances does the heartbeat 'touch' the parent's activity clock, and the touch description carries the child's live state ('subagent running <tool> (iteration i/max)'). When all three freeze for N cycles — 15 idle (450s) vs 40 in-tool (1200s), different because being inside a tool legitimately takes longer — tick() returns False, stopping the heartbeat so the parent's own watchdog is allowed to fire. The child is never killed by elapsed time; it is killed by demonstrable absence of progress.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Replace the wall-clock stopwatch in Halbert's subagent await with a progress-based staleness monitor. agents/state_machine.py:2022-2050 await_subagent_completion polls handle.status every 0.1s against a fixed `timeout: float = 300.0` deadline and on expiry simply breaks — a legitimately long subagent is declared over at 300s while a wedged one that finishes at 299s is declared fine, and no progress signal is consulted because SubagentHandle (agents/subagent.py:38-51) exposes none. Add a progress cursor to SubagentHandle (last_activity_epoch plus a coarse current_step, touched by the same on_event path _emit already owns at subagent.py:103-122), have the manager's periodic tick reset a staleness counter whenever it advances, define terminal-by-staleness with distinct idle vs in-work thresholds, and drop the fixed deadline. This is the precondition for C4/C5/C16 being meaningful.

missed_by_reader.title: Abandonment accounting: an unfinished child gets an explicit terminal entry, a cooperative stop signal and a deferred close — the parent never joins a wedged worker
missed_by_reader.lines: 97-146 (_run_children_parallel); with tools/delegate_tool_child_run.py:76-81 (_signal_child_stop), 333-360 (_defer_close_after_timeout), 776-816 (_ChildRun.cleanup)
missed_by_reader.mechanism: The parallel join polls with `_cf_wait(pending, timeout=0.5, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)` rather than as_completed(), explicitly 'so a wedged child cannot block the parent forever after an interrupt'. On a parent interrupt every still-pending future becomes a FABRICATED terminal entry — _fabricated_entry(idx, 'interrupted', 'Parent agent interrupted — child did not finish in time', child) — appended in input order, so an abandoned child is accounted for rather than silently missing. Abandonment is then a discipline: _signal_child_stop sends a cooperative request_hard_interrupt (falling back to setting _interrupt_requested) so the worker unwinds its own finally path; _defer_close_after_timeout refuses to close the child from the abandoning thread ('closing now could close SQLite under its final write — the done-callback is the first safe boundary') and instead shutdown()s the child's pooled sockets so a worker parked in an OpenSSL read settles with EOF, with one immediate sweep and one 5s re-sweep, because releasing FDs under a live SSL read corrupts native state; and _ChildRun.cleanup runs an explicitly ordered idempotent teardown (stop heartbeat, unregister, release credential lease, restore the parent's process-global tool names, detach from the interrupt list, close the child unless a timed-out worker still owns it).
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Fix the concurrency-slot leak this exposes. agents/state_machine.py:2044-2050: when await_subagent_completion's deadline passes it sets ctx.current_subagent_handle_id = None and yields the handle's still-non-terminal status, but the handle stays in SubagentManager._active forever because only complete() or cancel() remove it (agents/subagent.py:184, 203). With max_concurrent defaulting to 2 (subagent.py:89), two abandoned subagents permanently wedge the manager and _promote_next() never drains the queue again; worse, a real completion arriving after a cancel() returns False (subagent.py:184-187) and the result is silently dropped, while cancel() frees a slot without signalling the running work at all (there is no cancellation token on the handle). Give SubagentHandle a cooperative stop flag the runner polls, make the abandon path mark the handle terminal ('abandoned') so the slot is released and the queue drains, and never let a cancelled-then-completed handle drop its result.

missed_by_reader.title: Offloading background work to a thread must run in an EMPTY Context — asyncio.to_thread copies the caller's security ContextVars
missed_by_reader.lines: 21-34 (_run_in_fresh_context, _to_thread_process_service)
missed_by_reader.mechanism: The notifier/dispatcher loops never call asyncio.to_thread directly. Every blocking offload is routed through `Context().run(func, *args)` inside the thread, with the reason in the docstring: 'asyncio.to_thread copies the caller's context; a lingering delegate_task child marker would make write_txn false-trip for these process-owned writers. An empty Context keeps the DB guard intact for real children without exempting dispatcher writes.' The general rule: once a ContextVar carries an identity or a permission decision, any thread offload silently re-attributes the offloaded work to whoever happened to be on the loop, and the fix is an empty Context at the boundary rather than clearing the var (which would break the real children the guard exists for).
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Audit Halbert's thread-offload boundaries against its identity ContextVars. Halbert deliberately relies on context copying for propagation — tools/executor.py:42-50 documents current_turn_claim as using the 'same copy-down-the-task mechanism as current_turn_digest', consumed at the RoleGate inside executor.execute() to cap the effective speaker role — but nothing scrubs it at a thread boundary, and there are 20+ bare asyncio.to_thread sites, several security- or autonomy-adjacent: home/cognitive_loop.py:289 (the autonomous cognition tick), dashboard/routes/approvals.py:278 and :367 (proposal application), mcp/client.py:682/711/807 (outbound MCP posts), agents/state_machine.py:3656 and :3700. Each inherits whatever current_turn_claim / current_turn_digest (security/turn_digest.py:52) / current_speaker_role / current_turn_channel (agents/channels.py:246) / current_turn (continuity/provenance.py:59) was bound on the loop. Introduce one run_detached(fn, *args) helper that runs in a fresh contextvars.Context() and route every process-owned background offload through it, cognitive-loop tick first, so autonomous work is never attributed to — or exempted by — a user turn's identity. Deterministic-policy hygiene, exactly the no-LLM-in-security-decisions posture applied to propagation.

missed_by_reader.title: A positive denial marker that survives exec — absence of an identity key is never a grant — behind one predicate every gate uses
missed_by_reader.lines: 1-7 (module rationale), 71-74 (is_dispatcher_owned_worker_context), 76-92 (is_delegated_child_process_context, scrub_kanban_env), 101-112 (delegated_child_subprocess_env)
missed_by_reader.mechanism: Three rules worth taking as a set. (1) ONE PREDICATE: is_dispatcher_owned_worker_context() is documented as 'the single predicate every HERMES_KANBAN_* identity gate should use' — exactly one door, a pure boolean over context, no model involved. (2) ABSENCE IS NOT A GRANT: scrub_kanban_env removes the worker-identity env keys AND sets a positive marker HERMES_DELEGATED_CHILD_CONTEXT=1, because 'TASK absence alone would promote a descendant to an orchestrator' — dropping the key alone reads as 'this process is nobody's child', i.e. more privileged, not less. (3) THE FENCE CROSSES exec: delegated_child_subprocess_env carries the denial marker into real subprocesses, and 'the marker survives later execs, including scripts that remove TASK themselves'. It is also honest about its limits ('cooperative runtime scoping, not confinement of code with direct SQLite access'), and it uses a ContextVar rather than mutating os.environ because the worker's own claim heartbeat and concurrent readers share the process environment.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Halbert has no cross-process identity fence at all: streaming/pty.py:289-292 builds every spawned shell's environment as `child_env = dict(os.environ)` updated with an optional per-session env, and streaming/session_manager.py:99 passes env=None for the agent's own pool shells (streaming/agent_pool.py:83-88 spawns kind='agent-pool', watched=False), so a shell the machine runs for itself inherits the parent process environment wholesale — including anything the guest-persona lattice or a secure-context turn was meant to withhold, and any credentials in the daemon's env. Define one Halbert predicate (the persona/permission analogue of is_dispatcher_owned_worker_context) and a positive denial marker stamped into the env of every PTY/subprocess Halbert spawns on the agent's behalf, so a descendant is fenced by a value that is PRESENT rather than by a key that is missing and a guest-persona or secure turn cannot be escaped by one exec. Scope by capability boundary per the standing directive, and state the cooperative limits in the docstring the way the origin does.

missed_by_reader.title: A read ledger, so the parent is told when work it delegated wrote files it had already read
missed_by_reader.lines: 723-742 (append_sibling_write_reminder), 744-775 (emit_complete: files_read / files_written on the completion event)
missed_by_reader.mechanism: Hermes keeps both directions of file state per task id (tools.file_state: known_reads(task_id), writes_since(task_id, since, snapshot)). When a delegated child finishes, the parent's result entry is annotated with any file the child wrote that the parent had already read, as a literal '[NOTE: subagent modified files the parent previously read — re-read before editing: …]' appended to the summary (or a structured stale_paths list when there is no summary), capped at 8 paths with a '+N more'. The check deliberately looks at writes by ANY non-parent task_id, not just this child's, 'so nested orchestrator→worker chains are covered too'. The same read/write sets ride out on the subagent.complete progress event alongside tokens, cost and a tool-output tail, every field optional so the client degrades.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Halbert has only the write half. continuity/provenance.py:131 record_file_change is the write ledger (called from tools/write_config.py:95 and :160, tools/executor.py:1093, config/watcher.py:164), keyed to the turn via the current_turn ContextVar (agents/state_machine.py:1231-1239) — but nothing records what the machine READ, so 'the file you are about to edit changed under you' is not computable. This matters more here than in the origin: the founder runs concurrent sessions against this repo, user shells are watched rather than owned (DECISIONS.md:14), and config/watcher.py already observes external edits. Record reads into the same provenance ledger keyed by turn (or by watched-session id), then emit a stale-read note when a path the current turn read has been written by anything else since — surfaced in the conversation, not as a dashboard row.

missed_by_reader.title: The steer/completion linearization boundary: a steer that loses the race is recorded, never silently swallowed
missed_by_reader.lines: 376-385 (_merge_late_steer), 40-44 (_append_missed_steer), 616-631 (finish_failed / close_steering); with tools/delegate_tool_registry.py:50-56 and 107-121 (accepting_steer under the registry lock)
missed_by_reader.mechanism: Steering a running child races its completion, and Hermes closes that race explicitly. A registry record carries an accepting_steer flag set at registration and flipped under the single _active_subagents_lock; steer_subagent refuses the moment it is down (delegate_tool_registry.py:113-115). _merge_late_steer is documented as 'the linearization boundary for registry steering: from here the child cannot consume another steer. Closing under the registry lock either rejects a concurrent caller or drains every accepted exact text into the result before callbacks/result assembly run' — an accepted-but-undeliverable steer lands in the result as pending_steer, and on the failure/timeout path _append_missed_steer writes it into the entry as missed_steer with the error text amended ('[steer did not land before the subagent stopped: …]'). Acceptance closes BEFORE the stop signal is sent (await_child docstring: 'a concurrent steer is drained into the entry or rejected, never lost').
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Halbert already holds the same invariant one level up — agents/steering.py:111-127 apply_steer_to_results states that when there is no tool result to steer into 'an arrival is never silently dropped … the caller's single replace-not-grow pending slot holds it for the next batch boundary'. Missing is the equivalent at the subagent boundary, and it is the prerequisite for candidate C16: before extending steer down into SubagentManager, add the accept/close flag and the missed-steer record so a founder redirect arriving as a subagent finishes is surfaced in the result ('this did not land') rather than disappearing. Small; ship it in the same change as C16 rather than after it.

missed_by_reader.title: The 0-API-call timeout dump: the one blind failure gets a structured artifact, and only that one
missed_by_reader.lines: 148-200 (_dump_subagent_timeout_diagnostic), 84-147 (_format_thread_stack, _diag_section, _diag_sizes, _diag_threads), 678-706 (call site and the three differentiated error strings)
missed_by_reader.mechanism: A child that times out having made ZERO API calls is uninspectable — 'timed out with no response', 0 api_calls, nothing recorded. So exactly that case (is_timeout and api_call_count == 0) writes one file, logs/subagent-timeout-<sid>-<ts>.log, containing configured vs actual duration, the goal capped at 1000 chars, the child's config attributes, its enabled_toolsets and loaded tool names, prompt/schema SIZES (not contents), the activity summary and the worker thread's stack — with a Notes section stating when the file is written and the three known causes (oversized prompt rejected by the provider, transport hang, stuck credential resolution). The discipline is that the artifact is scoped to the one blind failure mode; the parent-visible error is differentiated three ways (raised / timed out before first LLM call / timed out after N calls) with the diagnostic path appended, plus structured timeout_phase and timed_out_after_seconds fields on the result entry.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: When Halbert's subagent await gains a real terminal-by-staleness path (see the heartbeat item), give the never-started case its own artifact rather than a bare handle.error string: on a subagent reaching its staleness threshold with zero recorded progress, write one capped file under Halbert's data dir with the frozen agent_config_snapshot (already on the handle, agents/subagent.py:48), the task_goal, the scoped_sources, prompt SIZE not content (Tier-2 rule: never write the assembled prompt to disk), and the PTY session id / last command; then differentiate the surfaced error between 'never started' and 'stopped making progress after N steps'. Route the text through the existing response-redaction choke point before it hits disk, the way tools/delegation_live_log.py:63-70 does.

HM05-delegation-subagents-kanban.verify_summary: Verified all 19 candidates by opening every cited origin path at the cited lines. missed_by_reader.title: End-of-turn over-claim verifier: state deterministically which claimed effects did NOT land
missed_by_reader.mechanism: _record_file_mutation_result (177-213) watches every write_file/patch outcome for the turn: a failure stores {path: {tool, error_preview}} keeping the FIRST error per path, and a later success on the same path removes the entry, so the ledger holds exactly what was attempted and did not land. _format_file_mutation_failure_footer (246-270) renders it as a footer saying verbatim 'N file(s) were NOT modified this turn despite any wording above that may suggest otherwise', listing up to ten paths with their error preview, with every path backticked via _neutralize_footer_paths (236-243) so the gateway's file auto-attacher cannot pick a protected path out of the footer. missed_by_reader.mechanism: _begin_tool_execution ends with a checkpoint preflight run on the FINAL (post-middleware) tool arguments, inside contextlib.suppress so a checkpoint failure never blocks the tool: for write_file/patch it calls _ensure_file_checkpoint (77-89), which resolves the path exactly as the file tools will (against the task's live cwd, not the process cwd) and checkpoints the working directory containing it; for terminal it checkpoints the command's cwd only when _is_destructive_command(command) says so, labelling the checkpoint 'before terminal: <first 60 chars>' (929-933). missed_by_reader.title: Leak-safe cross-thread coroutine scheduling (close the coroutine when the loop refuses it)
missed_by_reader.mechanism: safe_schedule_threadsafe (20-41) wraps asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe: a missing or closed loop raises internally, and every failure path calls coro.close() before returning None, because a coroutine that is neither awaited nor closed emits a 'coroutine was never awaited' RuntimeWarning and leaks its frame (module docstring 1-8). It deliberately does NOT wrap future.result(): once the loop accepts the coroutine its lifecycle belongs to the loop. consume_detached_task_result (44-50) is the matching done-callback for a cancelled-and-detached task so the loop does not log 'exception was never retrieved'.

missed_by_reader.title: Iteration accounting that can be refunded, and a per-turn ceiling that is not five

Combined with C5's over-eager _already_called and C13's empty-args coercion, five is a tight budget for a local model that has to read a file, run a command, read the output and answer. Task: unify the two ceilings into one budget object with consume/refund, refund iterations spent on inline meta-tools and on iterations that ended in a validation refusal rather than a tool result, and revisit the cap. Bookkeeping rather than new behaviour — land it with C5/C13, not alone.

candidates.title: Bounded, atomic, single-flight cached download for any large local dataset file

candidates.title: Invalidate a cached capability probe on an observed failure signal, not on a TTL

origin_paths.what: Successful probe cached without expiry; invalidateCachedIMessagePrivateApiStatus explicitly called by the RPC client the moment a live call actually fails, so the stale-available verdict cannot outlive the bridge it describes

candidates.mechanism: Trust a verified-present capability indefinitely, but bust the cache the instant a live call surfaces evidence it died — cheaper than polling, correct where a TTL would miss a mid-window death.
candidates.why_solid: Deliberate, documented rejection of naive TTL in favor of tying invalidation to the one signal that matters.
candidates.halbert_evidence: capabilities.py CapabilityRegistry.probe() runs once at startup (line 346 docstring) with no invalidation path found anywhere in the file — a dead HA connection or local-LLM daemon stays reported available until restart.
candidates.task_proposal: Add an explicit registry.invalidate(cap_name) hook called from the HA client, local-LLM/secure-model provider, and audio/web probe failure paths.
candidates.risks: Must distinguish a capability-is-gone signal from a single transient failure to avoid over-invalidating.

verdict.notes: Origin verified including the call site the reader asserted but did not cite: private-api-status.ts:59-76 returns the cached entry unconditionally when expiresAt===0; :78-88 the comment states a successful probe is cached without expiry and 'leaves no way back once the bridge dies... The RPC client calls this when the bridge stops answering'; :86-88 invalidate deletes the entry. Single non-test caller is client.ts:329, inside the catch at :320-337 ('this is the one place that learns the bridge went away') — invalidate, attempt recovery, rethrow a described error. Halbert confirmed: capabilities.py:412-450 probe() runs the seven _PROBES (:330-338) once and caches; has() at :457-461 only probes when not self._probed; no invalidate/refresh path exists — reset_registry() at :504-507 is a test-only singleton reset, not a per-capability bust. candidates.title: User-pluggable local-CLI TTS provider: argv-only invocation, magic-byte format sniffing, output/stderr byte caps

candidates.title: HTML nesting-depth DoS guard before DOM-based parsing, plus invisible-Unicode stripping on extracted content

candidates.constraint_conflicts: None — extends the existing redaction/choke-point philosophy to ingestion.

Halbert does — integrations/observation_text.py:91-104 does unicodedata.normalize('NFC', value) then drops every category-'Cf' character, with a docstring at :75-81 naming zero-width spaces, soft hyphens and 'the bidi overrides behind Trojan Source', mapping Cc/Zl/Zp to spaces. The reader's grep missed it because the implementation is category-based, not literal-codepoint-based. What IS absent is the wiring: observation_text is imported only by integrations/system_event_mapper.py:100, integrations/home_assistant/ha_event_mapper.py:22 and integrations/frigate/frigate_event_mapper.py:23 (HA/Frigate observation titles). candidates.title: Bounded batch/depth/timeout limits on any tool accepting a list of sub-actions

anti_patterns.title: Do not replicate the browser extension's full multi-driver-mode CDP/Playwright/relay-daemon surface

OC21-extensions-device-media-desktop.summary: Read 34 substantive files across all 19 assigned directories, concentrated on cua-computer, document-extract, geolocation, imessage, tts-local-cli, web-readability, and a targeted slice of the much-larger browser directory, per FOCUS guidance to prioritize macOS host-steward mechanisms over generic chat-platform adapters. Neither prior OSS-review doc nor the master plan references any directory in this unit — genuinely fresh territory. The strongest finds cluster around three themes on-mission for Halbert: (1) trust boundaries for any future desktop-input-injection capability — frame/generation-bound screenshot authorization and SHA-256-pinned native-artifact verification are real gaps given Halbert already has AppleScript UI-scripting (risk-classified but not screen-state-bound) and read-only screen capture; (2) content-ingestion hardening extending Halbert's already-mature redaction posture — invisible-Unicode stripping and an HTML nesting-depth DoS guard for RAG scrapers is a confirmed, cheap, concrete gap; (3) local-first infrastructure matching 'local models pinned' — a local-CLI TTS provider bridge with argv-only invocation, and a bounded/atomic/single-flight download helper for RAG scraper caching. Two smaller well-evidenced findings (capability-cache invalidation on observed failure not TTL; the hashed-token ephemeral viewer pattern for staged-command review) round out the set. Anti-patterns are clear: browser's 617-file multi-driver CDP/relay surface and voice-call's public-webhook telephony stack both solve a fleet-of-arbitrary-configurations problem Halbert doesn't have; matrix/signal/mxc/nextcloud-talk/sms are confirmed thin re-export shims with little to lift directly.

missed_by_reader.title: One-time capability ticket bound to the requester's liveness, not just to a TTL

HM04-agent-learning-verification-review.summary: This unit is unusually rich and directly on-target for Halbert's stated wants. The single highest-value find is the verify-on-stop trio (C1 verification_stop.py + C2 verification_evidence.py + C3 verify/ runner/recipes) — a deterministic, non-LLM-judgment mechanism that blocks the agent from claiming code-edit work is done without fresh, staleness-aware evidence, which is precisely what Halbert asked for by name. Close behind: the curator snapshot/rollback safety pattern (C5, independently valuable even without the full curator lifecycle C6) and the local-model idle-deferral queue (C12), which solves a GPU/slot contention problem Halbert's pinned-local-model architecture will hit the moment any background LLM-assisted work (memory consolidation, skill review) gets added. The learning-graph family (C7/C8) fills a real gap — Halbert currently has zero UI for 'what has been learned,' despite already recording the raw signal (skill telemetry, memory files) it would need. Two zero-engine prompt commands (/learn C9, /plan C10) and one subagent command (/review C11) are cheap, high-leverage additions needing no new plumbing. The clearest anti-patterns are the pet mascot (violates the host-steward identity and no-emoji rule), the Hugging-Face trace-upload destination, remote OTLP/fleet-health telemetry, and speculative training-trajectory collection — all four are shaped for a multi-instance product with an external operator/consumer, which Halbert (single-user, single-host, no training ambitions) is not; each anti-pattern's underlying safety PATTERN (redact-or-refuse, fail-closed egress scrub) was still extracted as a separate, smaller candidate (C14, C17). Given the unit's size (6168 lines across the 18 top-level files, plus ~4500 more in verify/monitoring/pet), roughly 60% of raw line count was read directly with the rest grepped for structure; the largest unread files (curator.py's 1084-line transition engine and background_review.py's 1191-line replay/whitelist internals) are flagged for a follow-up pass since they likely contain more concrete sub-mechanisms beyond what a header-level read surfaced. Structured output was also written to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Volumes-4TB-BAD-Halbert/b0e3f0dd-594e-4bec-b7ce-4859472b38f8/scratchpad/wf-oss/HM04-agent-learning-verification-review.json.

missed_by_reader.title: The stop-gate chain itself: an ordered, fail-open set of turn-end gates that preserve and SHOW the model's attempted answer
missed_by_reader.mechanism: This is the module that makes C1 work, and it is absent from key_files_read AND from unread_areas — the reader lifted the nudge builder without the machine that runs it. When the model stops with a text answer, apply_stop_gates (:104-174) runs three gates in a fixed order — verify-on-stop, the pre_verify plugin hook, the kanban terminal guard — and the FIRST that returns a nudge wins, so gates never stack. Six invariants worth naming separately: (1) the attempted answer is kept as `pending_verification_response` (:121-127) as a budget-exhaustion fallback while `final_response` is cleared so the finalizer can distinguish 'a gate continued the turn' from 'the turn errored' (:118-120, #61631); (2) the attempted answer is emitted and persisted as an INTERIM assistant row before the nudge (:93-101 `_append_interim_answer`) — the gate never hides what the model tried to say, and only the nudge is flagged synthetic (:95); (3) the nudge is a USER-role row appended after the assistant row so role alternation holds (:110-111, :116); (4) each gate stamps its own `finish_reason` ('verification_required' / 'verify_hook_continue' / 'kanban_terminal_required') so the transcript records which gate fired; (5) every gate lookup is wrapped in try/except returning None on failure (:47-49, :74-76, :88-90) — a broken gate can never block an answer; (6) per-gate visibility is a deliberate decision: the verify gate logs at debug and stays silent on the terminal (:137-138) while the kanban gate emits a visible status (:165-168).
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Before or with C1, add a stop-gate seam to halbert_core/halbert_core/agents/state_machine.py at the RESPONDING/finalize edge (the same place that stamps turn_activity at :4033): a small ordered list of gate callables, each returning a nudge string or None, first-wins, each wrapped so a raising gate is a no-op. Port the four honesty/state invariants verbatim — keep the attempted answer as a fallback, emit it as an interim assistant message so the user sees the attempt, append the nudge as a separate user-role row, and stamp a per-gate reason on the turn. Halbert has none of this: grep 'stop_gate|pending_verification|finish_reason' over halbert_core/halbert_core/agents/*.py hits only llm_client.py:42/277/489, a response dataclass field with no consumer. Without this seam C1, C4 and any future turn-end policy have nowhere to attach.

missed_by_reader.title: Refuse to run a check that would destroy the live state it is checking — fail open on absence, fail CLOSED on uncertainty
missed_by_reader.mechanism: Before a `compose` recipe runs build or start, run_verify calls _compose_live_state_reason (:183-206), a read-only `docker compose ps --status running` probe, and REFUSES the whole verify pass when containers are live — because `docker compose build` + `up` replaces them on an image-hash change and destroys container-local state (a real incident, #103567, cited at :218-221). The precision is in the error handling, and it is a three-way split rather than the usual two: FileNotFoundError (docker not installed) returns None and PROCEEDS, because 'the build phase would fail the same way, so there is nothing to protect' (:187-189); a TimeoutExpired refuses with the uncertainty named — 'docker compose ps timed out after 15s; live containers cannot be ruled out' (:200-201); a non-zero exit likewise refuses with the stderr tail (:202-204). Absence of the tool is fail-open; inability to observe is fail-closed. The refusal is reported as a synthetic failed PhaseResult carrying the reason and the instruction to rebuild by hand (:231-241), so the caller gets a legible verdict rather than a silent skip.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Record this as a standing rule and apply it to paths that already exist. Halbert IS the host machine, so any self-check, doctor, restart or 'verify my own services' routine has exactly this shape: the probe disturbs what it measures. Audit halbert_core/halbert_core/scheduler/autonomous_tasks.py and the discovery scanners for actions that would restart or replace something live, and give each a read-only pre-probe with the three-way split — tooling absent proceeds, tooling present and quiet proceeds, tooling present but unobservable (timeout/error) REFUSES with the uncertainty named in the message. Nothing in halbert_core distinguishes 'nothing to protect' from 'cannot tell whether there is something to protect' today.

missed_by_reader.title: Halbert's run_command leaks orphan processes on timeout: no process group, and only the direct child is killed
missed_by_reader.mechanism: Hermes starts a project's own server with `subprocess.Popen(recipe.start, cwd=..., start_new_session=True, ...)` (:171) so the child owns its process group, then tears it down through _terminate_process_group (:126-160): resolve the pgid via os.getpgid, SIGTERM the whole group via os.killpg, wait 10s, SIGKILL the group, wait 5s more — with a Windows branch degrading to proc.terminate()/proc.kill() on the direct child because os.killpg does not exist there, and ProcessLookupError/PermissionError handled at every step. The teardown runs in a `finally` around the readiness poll (:176-181), so a failed or timed-out readiness check still tears the app down.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: This is a live defect, not a missing nicety. halbert_core/halbert_core/tools/executor.py:832-837 spawns the model's `run_command` with `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(command, stdout=PIPE, stderr=PIPE, cwd=cwd)` — no start_new_session — and the timeout/exception path at :902-909 calls `proc.kill()` on the direct child only. The child is a shell; anything it spawned (a dev server, a `make` subtree, a background `&` job) survives the timeout and keeps running on the host indefinitely. Halbert already does this correctly elsewhere: halbert_core/halbert_core/streaming/pty.py:269 calls os.setsid() and :342-445 implements a SIGTERM-then-escalate-to-SIGKILL reaper. Fix: add start_new_session=True to the create_subprocess_shell call and replace proc.kill() with a killpg-based group teardown modelled on pty.py's existing escalation ladder. For a steward that identifies as the machine, leaving orphans behind after its own timeout is the wrong kind of footprint.

missed_by_reader.title: Never punish state you have not observed: three rules that stop an autonomous time-based sweep from mutating on first sight
missed_by_reader.mechanism: The deterministic sweep carries three independent guards against acting on clocks it never watched. (1) Deferred first run (should_run_now:142-160): when `last_run_at` is absent the first observation SEEDS it to now, writes the summary 'deferred first run — curator seeded, will run after one interval', and returns False — so a fresh install or update never mutates the library on its first tick. (2) First-sight baseline seeding (apply_automatic_transitions:212-216): a skill with no persisted record gets seed_record_if_missing and is skipped this pass, anchoring its inactivity clock to NOW rather than the epoch — otherwise every newly installed built-in is instantly 90 days stale. (3) Absence of evidence is not staleness (:224-229): use_count == 0 with an anchor newer than the stale cutoff means skip (and reactivate if previously marked stale); the anchor itself falls back to created_at so a never-active item cannot self-archive (:218-222). A fourth, smaller rule: cron-referenced skills are treated as pinned (:201-203) because usage only bumps when a job fires, so a paused or rare job would age its own skill out.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Write these as explicit invariants into the SK-7 curator packet (.handoff/DESIGN-SKILLS-SYSTEM-2026-09-07.md:264), which today specifies 'drafts that go 30 days without a single activation receipt are curator-archived automatically' (:223) with no first-sight rule at all — halbert_core/halbert_core/skills/telemetry.py records read/matched/explicit events, but a skill installed yesterday has no history and a naive timestamp sweep would archive the entire builtin set on first run. Then audit the same shape wherever else Halbert ages state on a clock: scheduler/catchup.py, scheduler/restart_budget.py, and any memory decay path in the continuity store. The rule to record in DECISIONS.md: an autonomous sweep must distinguish 'observed inactive for N days' from 'never observed', and must defer one full interval after seeding a clock it just created.

missed_by_reader.title: Verify an LLM's self-report against the observed diff: the model's summary is a claim, the before/after diff and the tool-call audit are the evidence
missed_by_reader.mechanism: After the optional LLM consolidation pass, the curator does not trust the model's narrative. It diffs the skill name set before/after, then classifies every REMOVED name through three independent evidence sources reconciled by a documented precedence ladder. _extract_absorbed_into_declarations (:551-563) reads the model's own `absorbed_into` argument off each skill_manage(action='delete') call — authoritative, with `into == ""` an explicit prune. _classify_removed_skills (:499-523) is the tool-call AUDIT: a skill_manage call on a different, surviving-or-new skill whose file_path/content arguments reference the removed name is the absorption signal, and calls on the removed skill itself or on a skill that no longer exists are explicitly not evidence (:512-515). _parse_structured_summary (:526-549) parses the model's fenced ```yaml block, matching ```yaml specifically 'so a code sample the model quoted elsewhere is never mistaken for the summary' (:531). _reconcile_classification (:564-609) merges them so every removed item lands in EXACTLY ONE bucket and the row records WHICH source decided: declared absorbed_into wins; a model consolidation claim wins only when its target exists in `destinations`; a model naming a missing umbrella falls back to the audit's real finding while recording both ('tool-call audit (model named missing umbrella)' plus model_claimed_into); an audit-only finding is kept and marked 'model omitted from structured block'; anything with no evidence is pruned with source 'no-evidence fallback'.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Halbert's design lifts only the narrow half: DESIGN-SKILLS-SYSTEM-2026-09-07.md:218 takes the absorbed_into delete guard verbatim (with the same #29912 incident) but says nothing about diffing observed state against the model's report. Add the reconciliation ladder to the SK-6/SK-7 packet: whenever an LLM pass mutates a store, snapshot the key set before and after, audit the tool-call arguments for corroboration, parse the model's structured claim, and reconcile with a fixed precedence in which every changed item lands in one bucket carrying the name of the source that decided it. This is also the general answer to the rule Halbert already asserts in halbert_core/halbert_core/continuity/verdict.py ('nothing claims DONE without evidence') — a rule that currently has no machinery behind it for LLM-performed work.

missed_by_reader.title: A background fork sharing the live session id writes its own harness turn into the real conversation — which the next live turn re-reads as a standing instruction

The fix is a block of hard detachments applied before the fork runs (:850-854): `_persist_disabled`, `_session_json_enabled = False`, `_end_session_on_close = False`, `_session_db = None`, `_skip_mcp_refresh = True` (so a late-connecting MCP tool cannot break tools[] parity), `suppress_status_output = True`, plus in-place-only compaction via _detach_fork_compression (:871). A second isolation of the same kind at :921-923 gates the fork's memory tool on the profile's memory flags 'so a memory-disabled profile is never contaminated by the review LLM', and keeps write tools denied on the dispatch-side whitelist (:929-931) so autonomous maintenance can only go through the validating skill_manage path.

It bites Halbert harder than Hermes: the founder design is ONE continuous conversation with hidden topic threads and no session list, so there is exactly one place a stray harness turn can land, and halbert_core/halbert_core/agents/conversation_sqlite.py plus threads.py are shared process-wide. There is no exposure today — continuity/consolidation.py:95-133 is deterministic and writes through record_state to the state store, never into the conversation — which is precisely why the rule should be written into the SK-6 packet now: any fork sharing the session id for cache warmth must have persistence, session finalization, status output and the write plane explicitly detached, as a checklist in the packet rather than something the implementer rediscovers from a bug.

missed_by_reader.title: Dry-run as a first-class preview mode whose output IS the deliverable, feeding a human approve step
missed_by_reader.mechanism: CURATOR_DRY_RUN_BANNER (:236-260) prepends a fenced block to the curator's review prompt keeping every instruction identical except the mutating ones: skills_list and skill_view stay allowed ('read as much as you need'), skill_manage patch/create/delete and write_file/remove_file are forbidden, and — the load-bearing part — 'Your output IS the deliverable. Produce the exact same human-readable summary and structured YAML block you would produce on a live run — but describe the actions you WOULD take, not actions you took. A downstream reviewer will read the report and decide whether to approve a live run with `hermes curator run` (no flag).' It also instructs the model to confess an accidental mutation explicitly. The identical report shape between dry-run and live is what makes the preview checkable against the eventual result rather than a different artifact.
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Do NOT lift Hermes's instruction-only prohibition — Halbert holds the stronger version of the enforcement half already (commands from the UI are staged, never executed; tools/executor.py:603-612 returns requires_confirmation as a RESULT rather than blocking), and a prompt asking a model not to mutate is the weak form. What is worth lifting is the reporting discipline: a preview pass must emit the SAME structured artifact a live pass emits, differing only in tense, so the two can be diffed and the approval is against the actual plan. Apply it to the SK-7 curator's report and to the staged-command surface generally: today a staged command shows what will run, but there is no 'here is the report this pass would produce' artifact the post-run report can be checked against.

A wrong credential calls limiter.recordFailureAndDelay(ip, scope) (a delay, not just a counter), a correct one calls limiter.reset(ip, scope), and rejectIfRateLimited (:368-385) short-circuits with reason 'rate_limited' plus retryAfterMs. The distinction is what makes brute-force throttling survivable for a legitimate client that simply opens the page unauthenticated.

The contract is the load-bearing part (:103-108): 'The contract separates detect() (reports findings) from repair() (reports changes/diffs/side effects), which keeps a path open for a future doctor --fix --dry-run without turning lint checks into mutation planners.' Selection is orthogonal to severity (:111-115 — checks can be default-disabled yet still reachable via --all/--only, and 'default selection is not a severity level'), the JSON finding shape carries checkId, severity, message, optional path/line/column, source, target, requirement and fixHint (:126-128), and exit codes are threshold-based: 0 nothing at or above --severity-min, 1 findings met it, 2 the command failed before emitting any (:132-136).
missed_by_reader.task_proposal: Halbert already has the registry and most of the contract: halbert_core/halbert_core/findings/detectors/{acoustic_anomaly,dropin_conflicts,fstab_phantom,permissions_hygiene}.py each expose detect() -> List[Finding], findings/store.py:41-46 gives Finding a severity (info|warning|critical) and a SQLite store with a severity index (:106), and findings/proposal_generator.py:202-273 is the repair half — which, per the founder's staged-not-executed rule, only proposes. What is missing is the read-only machine-readable front door: add a `python -m halbert_core.cli.lint [--json] [--severity-min] [--only <id>] [--skip <id>] [--all]` that runs the registry without writing findings to the store, emits checkId + fixHint per finding (the fixHint composes directly with candidate C15's 'exact config key to change'), and exits 0/1/2 on the threshold. halbert_core/halbert_core/cli/ currently holds only check_breach/check_credential/compromise_detection/credential_validation — no doctor or lint entry exists. This is also the natural host for candidate C2's rule pack: one command the pre-push gate calls.

candidates.title: Rolling per-exchange micro-compaction instead of naive keep-recent extractive summary

origin_paths.what: full design doc: cursor, rolling summary, defrag, DB sync, failure handling, telemetry
MicroCompactionMixin: _resolve_compact_cursor, _find_one_exchange, _micro_summarize_one, _needs_defrag/_defrag_rolling_summary, _micro_compact

candidates.mechanism: After every turn, fold exactly ONE oldest un-absorbed exchange (assistant + its tool results, up to the next user message) into a single running summary via a small/fast auxiliary LLM call. A persistent cursor tracks the absorption point; if lost (fresh process/resume) it is recovered by scanning the transcript for the last summary marker rather than re-summarizing. User messages are architecturally never touched (an exchange starts at the assistant turn) so instructions are never paraphrased away. Only the newest summary marker is kept (earlier ones are strictly redundant and dropped as superseded). When the rolling summary itself crosses a token threshold it is defragged (re-summarized in place, no transcript splice, cursor untouched). A DB sync step atomically archives replaced rows and inserts the compacted set so a resume doesn't double-load. Three consecutive summarizer failures on the same exchange force the cursor past it (bounded retry) so one poison exchange can't stall every turn forever. Off by default because every pass rewrites already-sent history and breaks any cache prefix.
candidates.why_solid: Directly targets a documented, self-admitted gap in Halbert: context/watermark.py's own module docstring says its should_compact() trigger 'has NO production caller' and the actual shipping path (ContextAssembler.build_conversation_window) just hard-trims to a token budget with no LLM summarization at all; conversation/summarization.py's compress_conversation_history() is a static keep-recent + one-shot extractive (non-LLM) summary with no cursor, no incremental absorption, no crash-safe resume, and no DB-consistent archival. Micro-compaction's asymmetric guarantee (compact the assistant's narration, never the user's instructions) is exactly the fidelity Halbert needs for a single, indefinitely-long continuous conversation.
candidates.halbert_evidence: halbert_core/halbert_core/context/watermark.py:1-30 (docstring: 'should_compact... NO PRODUCTION CALLER... Nothing in the shipping path compacts on a trigger at all'); halbert_core/halbert_core/conversation/summarization.py:44-64 (should_summarize has 'NO CALLER outside tests'), :118-160 (compress_conversation_history is a single keep_recent split + create_simple_summary, no cursor/no LLM/no resume-safety); grep -rn 'micro_compact\|rolling_summary\|defrag' halbert_core/halbert_core found nothing.
candidates.task_proposal: Build a HalbertMicroCompactor that: (1) walks halbert's block-typed message list to find the oldest un-absorbed full turn (assistant + tool blocks, bounded by user messages); (2) merges it into a running summary via the utility model slot (never the main/vision slot); (3) persists a cursor + rolling summary alongside the session row in agents/conversation_sqlite.py, recoverable by scanning for the last summary marker on cold start; (4) replaces the absorbed span with one assistant-role marker, keeping only the newest marker; (5) wires archival through the existing SQLite active/soft-archive machinery so resume never double-loads. Gate behind a config flag (default off, matching Hermes's own default) since Halbert's one-continuous-conversation design makes cache-prefix churn from a local model's KV cache reuse the equivalent cost this trades against.
candidates.prerequisites: Halbert needs a working auxiliary/utility LLM call path for cheap merge calls (utility model slot already exists per master plan) and a transcript summary-marker convention compatible with agents/conversation_sqlite.py's active/soft-archive rows.
candidates.risks: Every pass invalidates local-model KV-cache reuse the same way it invalidates a cloud prompt-cache prefix, so on Halbert's local-first posture the tradeoff calculus differs from Hermes's (no metered discount, but real latency cost from cache-miss reprocessing) — needs its own measurement, not a copy of Hermes's numbers.

verdict.notes: ORIGIN CONFIRMED in full. hermes agent/micro_compaction.py:38-59 (_resolve_compact_cursor + marker rehydration on resume), :61-88 (_find_one_exchange; user rows never absorbed), :157-193 (_needs_defrag/_defrag_rolling_summary, in-place marker rewrite, no splice, cursor untouched), :199-260 (_micro_compact: cadence gate, defrag branch, _sync_micro_compact_to_db, telemetry), :263-280 (_record_micro_failure forces the cursor past a poison exchange). Docstring :1-6 confirms OFF by default because every pass breaks the cache prefix. HALBERT EVIDENCE MISREAD: the reader read dead-code docstrings and concluded nothing summarises. The shipping answer is deliberate and different — context/assembler.py:1327-1332 says in code 'There is deliberately no summarisation branch here any more: the thread receipt is that summary and a better one — built by the ThreadManager from the whole subject'. agents/receipt.py:1-8 and :186-206 build_receipt is a deterministic nine-line extractive summary of the whole thread, refreshed at EVERY end_turn (agents/threads.py:470), so dropped-oldest turns are not lost. Replacing that with a rolling LLM summary violates 'never a model where a template suffices' with no clean degeneration. The transferable part — the absorption cursor, so the summary is not rebuilt from the whole thread each turn — is surfaced in missed_by_reader as a deterministic task, since _refresh_receipt is O(thread length) per turn (threads.py:1044-1049, receipt.py:196-206).

candidates.title: Deterministic per-tool-type one-line result summarizer as a cheap pre-LLM prune pass

origin_paths.what: _summarize_tool_result dispatch + _sum_terminal/_sum_write_file/_sum_search_files/_sum_browser/_sum_web_extract/_sum_delegate_task/_sum_execute_code/_sum_skill_view/_sum_clarify templates, never-raises guard

candidates.mechanism: Before falling back to an LLM summarization call, old tool-result messages are replaced with a deterministic, no-model, tool-type-specific one-line fact string built from the tool's own arguments and result ("[terminal] ran `npm test` -> exit 0, 42 lines output", "[write_file] wrote to src/x.py (12 lines)", "[search_files] content search for 'foo' in . -> 7 matches"). Every summarizer function is wrapped so a malformed historical call degrades to a byte-count string instead of crashing compression.

This is directly in the founder's deterministic-first spirit (same instinct as 'Tier 2 = template, never a model where a template suffices') applied to a different problem (compaction, not secrets).
candidates.halbert_evidence: halbert_core/halbert_core/context/watermark.py:80-110 (tool_result_truncate is a flat char-prefix truncation with no per-tool-type templating); grep -rn '_summarize_tool_result\|per.tool.*summar' halbert_core/halbert_core found nothing.

candidates.title: Stale outbound tool-result image eviction (keep-newest-N, placeholder the rest)

origin_paths.what: _retire_stale_tool_result_images / evict_stale_outbound_tool_images: walk tool messages newest-first, replace image parts on older ones with a text placeholder past a keep_newest cutoff

candidates.mechanism: On the per-request outbound message copy (not the persisted transcript), tool-result messages carrying image parts are scanned newest-first; only the newest N image-bearing tool results keep their image bytes, everything older gets a text placeholder ("[Attached image — stripped after compression]"). Runs on EVERY request, independent of whether compaction fired this turn, because a reactive 413-triggered strip is too late — stale screenshots otherwise ride every subsequent request until the provider rejects the payload size.
candidates.why_solid: Halbert has a rich vision_tools.py (screenshot/webcam/window capture, OCR) whose results plausibly carry image payloads into conversation history for a vision-capable model turn. Nothing in Halbert's context/watermark.py or context/assembler.py distinguishes image-bearing tool results from text ones, so repeated screenshot captures in a long single continuous conversation would accumulate un-evicted image bytes in every subsequent request.
candidates.halbert_evidence: grep -rn 'stale.*image\|image.*evict\|keep_newest' halbert_core/halbert_core found nothing outside watermark.py's plain-text truncation; tools/vision_tools.py:1-900 (capture_screenshot/capture_webcam/capture_window_tool etc.) has dedup-by-hash for re-capture but no retention policy for how many past captures stay embedded in conversation history sent to the model.
candidates.task_proposal: Add an outbound-only (never persisted) image-retention pass to context/assembler.py's request-building path: keep the newest N vision-tool-result images verbatim, replace older ones with a placeholder string, mirroring evict_stale_outbound_tool_images's newest-first scan and keep-newest cutoff.
candidates.prerequisites: Needs to know Halbert's tool-result content shape for image parts (agents/blocks.py block types) to identify which parts are images.
candidates.risks: Must run on the per-call copy only, never on the row Halbert persists to SQLite, or a legitimate historical screenshot becomes permanently unrecoverable from the durable record.

verdict.notes: ORIGIN CONFIRMED: agent/context_compressor.py:1229-1245 (_retire_stale_tool_result_images, newest-first, keep_newest cutoff, user uploads untouched), :1248-1263 (evict_stale_outbound_tool_images — 'Do not pass persisted history — the rewrite is send-path only'), :1212-1219 (_strip_images_from_tool_msg). HALBERT SCOPE CORRECTED AND MUCH SMALLER. Halbert never embeds images in persisted history: they ride a per-turn parameter (agents/states.py:193 images on StateContext, built fresh per process() at state_machine.py:668-689) and the thread store holds content as a plain string (assembler.py:1353-1355). No cross-turn accumulation. The real, smaller version: ctx.images is appended without any cap at state_machine.py:2538-2539 and :3521-3525, and the whole list is re-sent on every LLM call in that turn (:2622, :3940, :3965), so multiple captures in one turn re-send every frame each loop iteration. A keep-newest cap on ctx.images is worth it; the persisted-vs-outbound machinery is not.

candidates.title: Prompt-injection scan on loaded context files (block, don't warn)

origin_paths.what: _scan_context_content: runs _scan_for_threats(content, scope='context') on AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules/SOUL.md before injection; a hit BLOCKS the whole file with a visible marker, never partially redacts

candidates.mechanism: Any file that is about to be concatenated verbatim into the system/context prompt (project AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, a soul/identity file) is scanned with a 'context'-scoped threat detector before it enters the prompt. A match blocks the entire file (replaced by a '[BLOCKED: ... potential prompt injection]' marker) rather than warning after the fact, because by the time a warning would fire the content has already reached the model.
candidates.why_solid: Halbert already loads external project/context documents into prompts (prompts/context.py's context-injection formatters, dashboard/routes/development.py) and is mid-way through an explicit security-hardening pass (186 confirmed SEC findings, remediation branch). A file the host reads off disk and feeds verbatim into a system prompt is exactly the class of injection surface the ongoing security audit is meant to close, and nothing in the codebase currently scans loaded context docs before they reach the model.
candidates.halbert_evidence: grep -rn 'prompt injection\|injection scan\|scan_context\|suspicious.*instruction' halbert_core/halbert_core found only prose docstring mentions in integrations/modality_wiring.py and prompts/context.py's own comments — no actual scanning/blocking function.
candidates.task_proposal: Add a context-file threat scanner (reusing/extending Halbert's existing security/echo-guard scanning primitives if any exist) gated in front of every place halbert_core reads a project doc, AGENTS/CLAUDE-equivalent, or user-supplied file into a system/context prompt block, blocking (not warning) on a match.

candidates.risks: An overly aggressive scanner blocking legitimate project docs (false positives) is worse than doing nothing if it silently degrades context quality without visible signal — needs a visible chat-facing warning, matching Hermes's pattern of surfacing truncation/block warnings in the actual response, not just logs.

candidates.title: Progressive subdirectory AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md hint loading on first tool-touch

origin_paths.what: SubdirectoryHintTracker: as the agent navigates into subdirectories via tool calls, load AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules from newly-touched directories and append to the tool result, deduped by content digest, capped at 32KiB, within-working-dir guard, excluded-dir-name filter

candidates.mechanism: Rather than loading every project-doc file at startup (expensive, and most of a large repo's subdirectory docs are irrelevant to a given session), the tracker watches tool-call arguments (path/file_path/workdir keys, and shell command tokens) for newly-visited directories and appends that directory's first matching hint file to the TOOL RESULT (not the system prompt), so the content arrives exactly when relevant and never touches the cached prompt prefix. Ancestor directories up to 5 levels are also checked so reading a deep file still surfaces a parent AGENTS.md. Content already seen (by SHA-256 digest, catching symlink/copy duplicates) is never resent.

candidates.halbert_evidence: grep -rn 'subdirectory.*hint\|AGENTS.md\|CLAUDE.md' halbert_core/halbert_core --include=*.py found no matches for a progressive/on-tool-touch loader (only this project's own root-level CLAUDE.md is referenced via the SourcePrep skill-context import, not from inside halbert_core's own prompt assembly).

candidates.title: Side-question (/btw) answered without disturbing the main thread

origin_paths.what: answer_side_question: cache-parity fork of the live agent with tools denied at dispatch, falls back to a rendered-transcript one-shot when no live parent agent exists

candidates.mechanism: A user's quick tangential question is answered by forking the LIVE parent agent (reusing its warm KV/prompt-cache prefix, denying every tool call at dispatch by installing an empty thread-scoped tool whitelist so the fork can never mutate anything) and running a short synthetic prompt against the existing conversation snapshot — never appending a synthetic turn to the real transcript, never risking role-alternation, never invalidating any cache. If no live parent agent is available (host evicted it), it falls back to rendering a char-budgeted transcript digest and answering via a one-shot auxiliary call instead.
candidates.why_solid: This is close to a direct mechanism match for Halbert's own stated design direction: 'one seamless chat, hidden topic threads, recall by relevance, NO conversation list' (halbert-continuity-direction-2026-08-26 memory) — answering a side question without disturbing (or forking a visible thread off) the main conversation is exactly the UX problem hidden topic threads are meant to solve, and Hermes has already built and tested a working mechanism for it.
candidates.halbert_evidence: grep -rn 'side_question\|/btw\|answer.*without.*disturb' halbert_core/halbert_core found nothing; agents/threads.py implements topic threads as a persisted structural concept (thread rows, ephemeral flag) but no live in-memory cache-parity fork for a tangential answer.
candidates.task_proposal: Build a Halbert equivalent that forks the live agent state (denying tool execution for the fork) to answer a tangential question against the current conversation snapshot without writing a visible turn into the main thread, as a building block for the 'hidden topic thread, recall by relevance' UX the founder has already directed toward.
candidates.prerequisites: Needs Halbert's agent runtime to support an in-memory fork/snapshot concept (may already exist for delegate_task-equivalent subagent work — check agents/ for a fork/spawn primitive) plus a thread-scoped tool-denial mechanism.
candidates.risks: Usage attribution (tokens/cost) must be folded back onto the parent session, not lost or double-counted — Hermes explicitly does this via _record_review_usage_to_parent; skipping it would make cost/telemetry silently wrong.

candidates.title: Two-stage deterministic + LLM-upgrade thread title generation onto Halbert's existing provenance ladder

origin_paths.what: derive_title (instant, no model, never fails) then generate_title (JSON-schema-constrained small-model call), provenance precedence derived<llm<user, answer-shaped-output rejection guard, machine-authored-opener exclusion, control-wrapper stripping

candidates.mechanism: Stage 1 is a purely deterministic 'first meaningful line, trimmed to a word boundary' title, computed before any model call and guaranteed not to fail — written immediately so a session is never untitled. Stage 2 fires later with a small/cheap model call (JSON-schema-constrained response, thinking off) to upgrade to a proper 3-7 word title; it only ever overwrites a lower-authority title (derived), never a title the user or a higher-authority process already set. An answer-shaped-output guard rejects (not truncates) a title the model 'answered' instead of titled (more than 12 words), so a chatty small model can't leave half an assistant reply as the session name. Machine-authored openers (compaction markers, model-switch notices) are excluded from titling entirely.

Even under the 'no conversation list' UX ruling, titles remain useful for internal recall-by-relevance indexing and for the FTS full-text search Halbert already runs over conversations.

candidates.title: Replay-history repair for a turn that died mid-tool-loop (orphan/dangling tool_call tails)

origin_paths.what: strip_interrupted_tool_tails / strip_dangling_tool_call_tail / sanitize_replay_history: on resume, an interrupted or unanswered assistant(tool_calls) block is stripped (read-only tools) or kept with an UNKNOWN-effect orphan-recovery notice (side-effecting tools)

candidates.mechanism: A turn that died mid-tool-loop (process restart, stale timeout, interrupt before the tool result was written) leaves a dangling assistant(tool_calls) or an interrupted assistant->tool tail in the persisted history. Without cleanup, on resume the model sees an unanswered tool call and naturally re-issues it — which, if that tool call is itself what killed the host (e.g. a service restart command), causes an infinite reboot loop. The fix distinguishes side-effecting from read-only tool calls: read-only orphaned blocks are silently dropped; side-effecting ones are KEPT but their result is rewritten as an explicit 'this tool may have executed before Hermes stopped; its effect is UNKNOWN — inspect state before retrying' notice, so the model is warned rather than blindly re-issuing a possibly-already-executed destructive action.
candidates.why_solid: Halbert already has 'interrupt algebra (stop/steer/redirect, generation claims)' lifted, plus a 'terminal is watched by the AI' design and execute_code with host-side RPC — all surfaces where a tool call can be interrupted mid-flight by a restart, a daemon crash, or a user Ctrl-C. Nothing in the codebase currently distinguishes an interrupted side-effecting tool call from a read-only one on resume, which is exactly the reboot-loop failure class Hermes hit and fixed (#49201 per the module).
candidates.halbert_evidence: grep -rln 'dangling\|orphan.*recover\|interrupted.*tool_call\|tool_calls.*interrupt' halbert_core/halbert_core found continuity/write_guard.py and agents/migrations.py — but agents/migrations.py:255 _sweep_orphaned_partials is import/migration bookkeeping, an unrelated concept (dropping half-imported legacy-store threads, not repairing an interrupted live tool-call tail); no replay-time tool-call-tail sanitizer exists.
candidates.task_proposal: Add a resume-time sanitizer to Halbert's turn/thread-loading path (agents/threads.py or the conversation loader called on resume) that detects a trailing unanswered or interrupted assistant(tool_calls) block, drops it if every call was read-only, and otherwise keeps it with an explicit UNKNOWN-effect notice, using Halbert's existing tool side-effect classification (if any — check tools/executor.py) or adding one.
candidates.prerequisites: Needs a side-effecting vs read-only tool classification function (tool_may_have_side_effect equivalent) if Halbert doesn't already have one.
candidates.risks: This is a resume-path correctness fix, not a feature — skipping it silently leaves the exact reboot-loop failure mode latent in any Halbert surface that restarts mid-tool-call (host restart, scheduler daemon restart, terminal channel reconnect).

candidates.title: Stale dangerous-confirmation expiry (redact-in-place after a short window)

origin_paths.what: strip_stale_dangerous_confirmations: a matched dangerous-confirmation phrase ('confirm forced restart', 'confirm shutdown', etc.) in a timestamped user message older than 60s is redacted in place with an explicit expiry sentinel

candidates.mechanism: A short, fixed list of phrases that unlock destructive host actions (forced restart, shutdown, factory reset, 'yes delete everything', with i18n variants) is checked against every timestamped user message on replay. Any match older than 60 seconds is redacted IN PLACE (content replaced with an explicit '[A high-risk confirmation previously given here has EXPIRED and must not be acted on...]' sentinel) rather than deleted, preserving strict role alternation while making the confirmation unusable. This closes a specific incident class: a stale confirmation surviving in history reads to the model as still-valid when a later, unrelated message ('are you there?') arrives minutes afterward, and the model may treat the new turn as re-confirming the earlier destructive action.
candidates.why_solid: Halbert's dashboard/routes/terminal.py already has a CAUTION/DANGEROUS safety-tier system requiring explicit confirmation for destructive commands ('systemctl restart' etc.), and the founder's design has NO session boundaries (one continuous conversation) — which makes a stale confirmation MORE dangerous in Halbert than in Hermes, since there's no natural session-reset point that would otherwise clear it. Nothing currently expires an old confirmation.
candidates.halbert_evidence: halbert_core/halbert_core/dashboard/routes/terminal.py:55-497 (SafetyTier.DANGEROUS + requires_confirmation logic exists) but grep -rln 'confirm.*restart\|dangerous.*confirm\|confirmation.*expir' halbert_core/halbert_core found only streaming/injection_check.py and dashboard/routes/terminal.py's own definitions — no time-based expiry of a past confirmation in conversation history.
candidates.task_proposal: Add a stale-dangerous-confirmation redaction pass to Halbert's turn-loading/replay path, matching the DANGEROUS-tier command phrases already defined in dashboard/routes/terminal.py against timestamped history and redacting matches older than a short window (60s, or tuned to Halbert's actual confirmation UX latency) in place.
candidates.prerequisites: Needs message timestamps to already be reliably present on persisted turns (agents/conversation_sqlite.py already has a timestamp column per the schema).
candidates.risks: Given Halbert has no session boundary at all, this control is more load-bearing here than in Hermes (where a session eventually ends); the expiry window should be tuned conservatively and tested against the actual confirmation UI round-trip latency in dashboard/routes/terminal.py.

HALBERT ALREADY SOLVES THIS, STRUCTURALLY BETTER. Halbert never grants a destructive action by matching prose in history: a HIGH-risk action pauses the turn in AWAITING_CONFIRMATION and resumes only via the explicit confirm_action(session_id, confirmed) API (state_machine.py:1434-1441, :1353-1357), and any NEW message abandons the staged action — state_machine.py:834-855 _supersede_paused_turn and :857-917 _record_superseded_turn end the turn 'cancelled' recording 'not run — superseded' (sentinel matched by exact equality at receipt.py:76-82, :118-135 so systemd output containing the word cannot forge it). candidates.title: Streaming-safe stateful think/reasoning-block scrubber

origin_paths.what: StreamingThinkScrubber: per-delta feed()/flush() state machine that holds a partial open/close tag across chunk boundaries so a <think> tag split across two streamed deltas is never leaked into visible output

candidates.mechanism: A regex that strips <think>...</think> blocks is correct for a COMPLETE string but wrong when run per-delta on a token stream: an opening <think> tag that arrives alone in one chunk (before its content or closing tag) is invisible to a stateless per-chunk regex and leaks straight through to the user. The scrubber holds state across feed() calls (_in_block, a partial-tag buffer, and a 'last emission ended with newline' flag used to gate whether an open tag counts as a real block-start vs. prose that merely mentions '<think>'), and flush() at end-of-stream discards any content still inside an unterminated block (leaking partial reasoning is judged worse than a truncated answer) while emitting a held-back non-tag tail verbatim.
candidates.why_solid: Halbert's utils/reasoning.py:parse_thinking_blocks() is a batch regex parser over a COMPLETE string (`r'<think>(.*?)</think>'` etc.) — exactly the class of implementation this module documents as unsafe under streaming, because a non-greedy `.*?` with no closing tag simply fails to match and the reasoning content (or a lone opening tag) passes straight through unstripped. If Halbert streams model output token-by-token to any surface (dashboard chat streaming, TTS/voice pipeline, terminal channel) while using a local reasoning model (already a stated concern — utility/model slots), a leaked partial <think> tag or raw reasoning text is a real, demonstrated failure mode.
candidates.halbert_evidence: halbert_core/halbert_core/utils/reasoning.py:30-55 (parse_thinking_blocks uses complete-string non-streaming regex patterns `<think>(.*?)</think>` etc.); grep -rn 'think_scrubber\|StreamingThink' halbert_core/halbert_core found nothing — no stateful streaming variant exists.
candidates.task_proposal: Port the StreamingThinkScrubber state machine (feed/flush, partial-tag holdback, block-boundary gating) into utils/reasoning.py or a new streaming-specific module, and use it anywhere Halbert streams token deltas to a live surface (dashboard SSE/websocket chat stream, voice/TTS pipeline) instead of the current complete-string parse_thinking_blocks, keeping the latter for post-hoc/non-streaming parsing.
candidates.prerequisites: Needs to identify every streaming delivery path in Halbert's dashboard/integrations code that currently forwards raw model deltas.
candidates.risks: The block-boundary gate (an open tag only starts a block at stream-start/after-newline/whitespace-only-line-so-far) is the subtle correctness property — a naive port that strips any occurrence of '<think>' anywhere would over-suppress legitimate prose that mentions the tag name.

verdict.notes: ORIGIN CONFIRMED: agent/think_scrubber.py:1-8, :19-36 (five tag families, lowercased literal tags for the hot path, orphan-close regex), :41-45 reset, :47-52 _emit with the newline flag, :55-88 feed (partial-tag holdback, in-block discard, closed-pair vs boundary-open priority). Halbert has two stateful streaming strippers already: utils/reasoning.py:140-205 StreamingReasoningParser (all four tag families, assume_thinking_mode for templates that open implicitly) and an inline one in the live SSE path at dashboard/routes/agent.py:1234, :1441-1479 (in_think_block flag, 7-char holdback for a split '<think>', 8 for '</think>', final-buffer guard). candidates.title: ReDoS-safety structural validator + literal-prefix pre-screen for any pluggable redaction/regex pattern registry

origin_paths.what: _pattern_structure/_has_top_level_alternation/_has_nested_unbounded_repeat structural regex analysis, _PATTERN_REJECT_RULES, register_redaction_patterns' additive-only plugin registry with a literal-prefix pre-screen gate

candidates.mechanism: Any regex pattern registered into the redaction system (by a plugin, or by config) is statically analyzed BEFORE being compiled into the combined matcher: a single scan detects (a) top-level alternation that would defeat the literal-prefix guarantee the pre-screen relies on, and (b) nested unbounded quantifiers (`(a+)+` shape) which is the canonical catastrophic-backtracking ReDoS structure. Either rejects the pattern with a specific, actionable warning rather than silently degrading or crashing at runtime — important because registered patterns run on EVERY log line and tool output. A cheap substring pre-screen (the pattern's literal prefix) gates the expensive combined regex so most lines never pay the regex cost at all.
candidates.why_solid: Halbert's redaction is currently a known-secret echo-guard (SecretVariantRegistry: only redacts values it has already seen, e.g. from loaded config) with no general pattern-based scanning surface at all — so there is, today, no place this validator would even apply. But Halbert is actively building skills/ (CC-compatible SKILL.md with provenance, already lifted) and MCP tool surfaces, both of which are exactly the kind of third-party-extensible surface that eventually wants to register its OWN redaction patterns (a skill author knows their own tool emits a particular secret shape). The validator is the safety net that makes accepting such registrations safe rather than a standing ReDoS risk.
candidates.halbert_evidence: grep -rn 'ReDoS\|redos\|unbounded_quantifier\|catastrophic backtrack' halbert_core/halbert_core found nothing; halbert_core/halbert_core/ingestion/redaction_registry.py:32-98 (SecretVariantRegistry) has no regex-pattern-registration API at all, so there is no current attack surface for this to guard — but see C13 for the companion mechanism (proactive pattern redaction) that would introduce that surface.
candidates.task_proposal: If/when Halbert adds any pluggable regex-based redaction or scanning surface (own work, skill-declared, or MCP-server-declared), gate every registered pattern through this structural validator (top-level-alternation reject, nested-unbounded-repeat reject, literal-prefix-length-2 minimum) before it is ever compiled into a hot-path matcher.
candidates.prerequisites: Meaningful only once Halbert has a pattern-registration surface to protect — pairs naturally with C13.
candidates.risks: Low risk to adopt defensively even before it's strictly needed; the cost of the validator itself is negligible and it forecloses a whole bug class (a well-meaning skill author's regex hanging every log line) before it can exist.

verdict.notes: ORIGIN CONFIRMED: agent/redact.py:714-720 _extract_literal_prefix, :723-728 _skip_char_class, :731-741 _unbounded_quantifier_follows, :744-776 _pattern_structure (one scan for top-level alternation and nested unbounded repeat, with an honest note that overlapping branches like (a|aa)+ are not detected), :818-832 _PATTERN_REJECT_RULES (three rules incl. the 2-literal-prefix minimum the pre-screen needs), :835-868 register_redaction_patterns (additive-only, warn-and-skip, never raise).
